To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the number of convolution layers should not be increased beyond three, and that the number of feature channels should be kept low to preserve the information passed from one layer to another.
the number of convolution layers and feature maps in a convnet are two important factors in determining performance and complexity of the extracted features.

1) increasing the number of convolutions increases performance, but at the same time, the complexity of the features derived decreases with every additional convolutional layer, and 2) preserving the information passed through the layers is important in improving performance, and increasing the number of filters is less important.
In summary, our research is concerned with
investigating the impact of different convnet architectures on activity recognition and the derived features.

the following: 1) evaluating different convolutional network architectures for activity classification using smartphone data, and 2) understanding how the derived features change with each layer of the network.
evaluating different convolutional neural network architectures and their impact on the performance of activity classification.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best convnet architecture for activity recognition is one with a small number of convolutional and fully-connected layers, but with a large number of feature maps.
a convnet architecture that has a large receptive field, a large number of feature maps, and preserves as much information as possible would be a good choice for activity recognition.
the best performing architecture is a 4-layer deep convnet with the first two layers having 32 feature maps and the last two layers having 64 feature maps.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the number of feature map channels should be increased to improve the performance, but not to the point that the information passed from one layer to the next is lost.
a deeper network is not always better.
the number of convolution layers should be chosen carefully, and the information passed from one layer to another should be preserved.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of convnets can be further improved by increasing the number of layers and feature maps.
, for the activity recognition problem, the number of layers should not be increased beyond a certain limit.
the number of convolution filters should be carefully selected based on the complexity of the features that need to be extracted from the data.
